verdicts.rationale: Both are Dretske's 'Knowledge and the Flow of Information', 1981. Same title, author, year. Blackwell (UK) vs MIT Press (US) are co-editions of the same book; differing ISBNs reflect the two editions, not distinct works.

The 1981 book vs the 1983 'Precis of Knowledge and the Flow of Information', a separate short article in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (vol 6, pp 55-63) with its own DOI. The Precis is a distinct publication summarizing the book.
The 1981 book vs the 1983 BBS Precis article (same DOI as dretske1983pr). Book and precis are distinct works.
Both are Dretske 1981 'Knowledge and the Flow of Information'. MIT Press vs Blackwell are co-editions of the same book; differing ISBNs are edition-level, not distinct works.
The 1981 book vs the 1983 BBS Precis article with its own DOI. Distinct publications.
The 1981 book vs the 1983 BBS Precis article. Distinct publications.

Dretske's chapter 'Information-Theoretic Semantics' (pp 381-393, chapter DOI) vs the whole edited volume 'The Oxford Handbook of Philosophy of Mind' by McLaughlin, Beckermann & Walter. Shared ISBN is the container volume; chapter and book are distinct entries.
Both are Shimon Edelman, 'Computing the Mind', 2008, Oxford University Press, identical ISBN 978-0-19-532067-1. Note in a confirms the 'Internet FAX' title was a scanner artifact for the same book.

Two different Egan papers: 'Individualism, Computation, and Perceptual Content' (Mind 1992, vol 101) vs 'Computation and Content' (Philosophical Review 1995, vol 104). Different titles, journals, years, and DOIs.

Epstein's chapter 'The Metatheoretical Context' (pp 1-22) vs the book 'Perception of Space and Motion' (Epstein & Rogers, eds). The shared DOI is the chapter's DOI erroneously copied onto the book entry. Chapter and containing book are distinct.

Both are the 1956 Dover edition of Euclid's Elements (Heath translation). Title variants ('Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements' vs 'Thirteen Books of the Elements'), same year and publisher; b's publisher field captures the Heath/Dover second-edition detail. Same work.

Both are Euler's 'Lettres a une Princesse d'Allemagne', 1960, Teubner. Same title (minor spelling variant), author, year, publisher. The citekey euler1761 refers to original composition date but the fields describe the 1960 edition.

'Psychophysical evidence for a shared representational medium for mental images and percepts' (Farah 1985, vol 114) vs 'Electrophysiological evidence...' (Farah, Peronnet, Gonon & Giard 1988, vol 117). Different titles, years, author lists, and DOIs; parallel companion papers, not the same work.
Same distinction as above: Farah 1985 psychophysical paper vs the 1988 electrophysiological paper. Different DOIs and years.
Farah 1985 psychophysical paper vs 1988 electrophysiological paper. Different titles, years, DOIs. Distinct works.

Both are Feldman, 'What is a visual object?', Trends in Cognitive Sciences 2003, vol 7(6):252-256. Entry a's title has the journal citation appended into the title field, but the volume/number/pages match exactly. Same article.
Both are Feldman 2003 'What is a visual object?', TiCS 7(6):252-256. Same article as feldman2003visual (identical DOI target).

'Mental imagery acuity in the peripheral visual field' (Finke & Kosslyn 1980, JEP:HPP, vol 6) vs 'Mapping the visual field in mental imagery' (Finke & Kurtzman 1981, JEP:General, vol 110). Different titles, journals, co-authors, and DOIs.
Both are von Fintel, 'The presupposition of subjunctive conditionals', 1998, in The Interpretive Tract, pp 29-44 (b has a typo 'presuppositon' and lists 25 as volume vs number). Same chapter.

Both are Firestone & Scholl, 'Enhanced visual awareness for morality and pajamas? Perception vs memory in top-down effects', Cognition vol 136, pp 409-416. Entry a scrambled title/journal fields and lists 2014 (online) vs b's 2015 (print), but same volume, pages, and work (DOI 10.1016/j.cognition.2014.10.014).
